segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: easy English to help you learn. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. Go to our website to find a script for this episode to read along,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: as well as a worksheet with questions on the programme.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello Beth, how are you doing today?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I am very well, thank you, Neil. How are you doing?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm pretty good. What are we talking about today?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, today we are talking about our plans for the future.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Beth, do you like to make plans for the future?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Um, no, I don't like to make lots of plans, but I think it's good to have some plans. What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I have, let's say, dreams about the future.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But not really plans. So, things I'd like to do maybe in the next few years.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK well I am interested to hear about your dreams So what are your plans for the future

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well in the next few years my kids will probably leave home because they growing

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: up and so I'll have a lot more time. And I would like to do things I don't do very much

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: now. So when they leave home, I'll spend more time going for walks in the countryside or

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: playing music or cooking nice meals.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Okay, that sounds really good. Yeah, good plans.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you, Beth? Do you have any goals in your life?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, there's a few things that I want to do. So, for example, if I can, I want to move to a bigger

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: house. Hopefully if I can I will move to the countryside because at the moment I live in a

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: place where there are quite a few other houses but I would really like to be out with more fresh air

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and places to go walking more easily. Is there anything Neil that you have always wanted to do

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but you haven done yet like travel somewhere or do something crazy like skydiving

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes there are always interesting places in the world to visit that I haven visited so far I

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: think also I would really like to get very, very good at a foreign language.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, that is a good goal.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Because at the moment I can speak bits of language, but nothing really impressive.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, okay. Yeah, I think I have similar goals. If I have the time, I'll travel to some other countries and practice speaking different languages a bit better than I can do at the moment. But it's difficult with time and money. Travelling is expensive. So we'll see.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: One day, Neil, we will both be retired

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Have you got any thoughts on what you want to do when you're retired?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I know it's not yet

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, but it's a bit closer for me than you

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It's difficult to think what I would like to do with all that free time

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I think it important to have a plan rather than just sit on the sofa watching TV all day

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: You better start thinking then

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the language we used during our conversation.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We had goals, things you want to do or complete.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we talked about future plans using the first conditional with when.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: For example, Neil, when your children leave home, you'll play more music and go on walks.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we used the first conditional using if to talk about future possibilities.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes, I said that if I can, I will move to a bigger house.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Remember there's lots more to help you with your English on our website.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Try our video series, The London to Edinburgh Challenge,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: where you can practice easy English with an exciting race.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Visit bbclearningenglish.com to find

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: all of the episodes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Next time, we'll talk about television and the things we like to watch.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye.
